newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill both repo and spot rates end up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill both repo and spot rates end up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Monday due to gains in the domestic A share market today and tight fund supplies, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract surged to 26.80 percent on Monday from 14.01 percent last Friday.
Total turnover increased to nearly 12 million lots from 7.96 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.

"Active trading on the domestic A share markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen have stimulated more buying on the repo market," said one trader. "The listing of Diamond Co in the Shanghai Stock Exchange also increased the demand for funds."
"The sharp rise in the three-day contracts partly resulted from some financial institutions borrowing funds for the year-end settlement before Wednesday," said a second trader.
Traders expect the repo rates to stay at high levels on Tuesday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on rumours of a cut in bank interest rates early next year.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 117.58 yuan from 116.68 yuan on Friday. Turnover on the bond was 1.03 billion yuan.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market rose to 1.22 million lots from 1.02 million.
"The word in the market is that the central bank will cut bank interest rates in the first quarter next year," said a local trader.
